scientific_scope.statement: With grids, across and down words (maximal contiguous white runs, length 1 allowed), complete rook placements (exactly one selected white square in every across and every down word), |RP(G)| as the number of complete subsets of the white squares, w in S_n as a bijection of {1..n}, and Grid(w) with black squares (i, w(i)), all defined in general: not_conjecture310 : not Conjecture310, where Conjecture310 := for all r > 0, ((exists n >= 1 and w in S_n with |RP(Grid(w))| = r) iff (r != 4 and r != 12 and r mod 4 != 3)). Witness w = 2 7 4 8 1 6 3 5 in S_8: w8_isPerm, words8 (14 across and 14 down words computed from w), squares8 (56 white squares), rpCount_G8 : |RP(Grid(w))| = 155, mod_155 : 155 mod 4 = 3. The count is defined by brute-force take-or-skip enumeration of all 2^56 sub-selections and computed by a pruned search proved equal to it for every grid (rpCount_eq_pr); rpCount_faithful proves for every grid that the enumerated candidates are the subsets of the white squares, each exactly once. No permanent, matrix or matching graph is entered or used.
scientific_scope.outcome_scope: FULL for Conjecture 3.10 of arXiv:2609.03081v1 as stated (an equivalence for every positive integer r): the 'only if' half fails at r = 155, which refutes the equivalence. The 'if' half, the status of 4 and 12, and any corrected classification are untouched. One finite instance is a complete refutation here because the statement is universal in r with no asymptotic clause.
binding_points: What is counted: 'rook placement count' is |RP(Grid(w))| with COMPLETE placements ('Henceforth ... by a rook placement, we mean a complete non-attacking rook placement'). Under the reading 'all non-attacking placements' the witness does NOT refute (28,666,418 = 2 mod 4); that reading is excluded by the source's wording and numbers (it gives 2936 for 2 5 3 1 4, which the source says has exactly one) and would make the conjecture false at n = 2 anyway (4 placements). This point carries the most weight.

Cardinality: rpCount is a brute-force count over sub-selections of the white-square list; rpCount_faithful proves for every grid that these are the subsets of the white squares, each exactly once; the pruned search used for the computation is proved equal to the brute-force count for every grid.
Words of length one are words (the source declines a minimum word length); the witness grid has four of them and they force four rooks.
Index convention: black squares at (i, w(i)), one-based, matrix convention. The transposed convention gives the same count (certified); inverse, reverse and complement give 155 by symmetry (Python).
One instance suffices: the conjecture is an exact classification for every positive integer r, with no asymptotic clause; the refuted half is 'only if'. Conjecture310_onlyIf isolates it.

Non-vacuity and calibration: thirteen values stated in the source are reproduced by the same definitions in the kernel (n!, n!-(n-1)!, 0 for an edge square, the interior-square formula, the two grids of display (2.1), 2 5 3 1 4 -> 1, 2 4 1 3 -> 2, 2 6 3 1 5 4 -> 5, 2 5 1 4 3 -> 6, 2 1 4 3 -> 5).
scientific_scope.not_claimed: Nothing about whether 4 or 12 occur, nothing about the 'if' half, no corrected spectrum. Minimality of n = 8, 'exactly 32 permutations' and 'only 155, 191, 195 in S_8' are uncertified C++ output. Not that the counterexample lay beyond the authors' computation: it lies inside their stated range n <= 8. The source's identity |RP(G)| = perm(B_G) and the archived 9 x 9 residual-permanent argument are not formalised and not used. The two works the source cites for the word graph were not read. [After the adversarial review: one of the two, Coté and Merrill (arXiv:2109.05094), has since been searched and is irrelevant; the McSweeney chapter remains unread. Not claimed either: that 155 is the smallest exceptional value, except 'for n <= 9, by uncertified enumeration' (reviewer).]
scope_sentences_to_carry_with_FULL: The witness lies inside the source's own stated exhaustive range (n <= 8), above the range of values (r <= 108) the source reports; the curator restatement given to the model omitted that sentence. It is not a counterexample beyond the authors' reach.
Only the 'only if' half of the equivalence is refuted; the 'if' half, the status of 4 and 12 and any corrected classification are untouched.

Minimality of n = 8, 'exactly 32 permutations' and 'only 155, 191, 195 in S_8' are uncertified enumeration; '155 is the smallest exceptional value' only 'for n <= 9, by uncertified enumeration' (reviewer).
